Philosophe et mathématicien de Leipzig,: A philosopher and mathematician from Leipzig, he invents calculus at the same time as Newton. In 1673, he presents to the Royal Society a machine that multiplies, thanks to its stepped drum. He also studies binary calculation, which he publishes in 1705.
Né à Lyon en 1752, il brevète en 1801 un: Born in Lyon in 1752, he patents in 1801 a mechanism that reads the pattern of a fabric from punched cards. The canuts, who fear for their jobs, at first jeer at him. His cards will inspire Babbage's Analytical Engine.
Mathématicien anglais, il conçoit dans l: An English mathematician, he designs in the 1820s a machine to calculate tables, then in 1837 describes the Analytical Engine, with a mill that calculates and a store that remembers. He finishes none of his machines. He tells his life story in 1864 in Passages from the Life of a Philosopher.
Ingénieur et mathématicien américain, il: An American engineer and mathematician, he shows in 1937, in his master's thesis at MIT, that Boolean algebra describes relay circuits. He then founds information theory. He also loved juggling and building whimsical machines.
Mathématicienne et officière de la marin: A mathematician and US Navy officer, she programs the Harvard Mark I from 1944. In 1952, she completes the A-0 system, one of the first compilers, and her work then leads to the COBOL language. She leaves the Navy in 1986 with the rank of rear admiral.
